mechanism.owner_quote: A gateway can centralize routing, quotas and common policy.
mechanism.reason: Explains the gateway's centralizing role for shared edge concerns.

invariant.owner_quote: Keep resource authorization at the boundary owning the resource, with documented delegation if a central decision service is used.
invariant.reason: Requires domain authorization to remain at the resource-owning boundary.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: Gateway bypass, configuration drift, a stale route and an outage that blocks every backend are common.

alternative.owner_quote: A BFF, a service-mesh sidecar or direct backend exposure with an explicit identity contract may be preferable when the gateway adds a shared bottleneck without a required central policy.

mechanism.owner_quote: Gateway routing is an edge contract over a versioned route table: a gateway matches request attributes to a route and applies policy, each route binds match predicates to a backend and a policy version, and the table changes independently of the backends.

invariant.owner_quote: Describe separately the externally resolved name, the service membership view, the connection destination and the backend selected for each request.
invariant.reason: Requires the four routing concerns to remain separately described.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: Stale routes, ambiguous matches and bypass around the gateway are common.

alternative.owner_quote: A reverse proxy, client-side discovery or a BFF may be preferable when routing policy is simple or the gateway would become a hidden shared dependency.

mechanism.owner_quote: Gateway aggregation composes several owner responses into one client response at the edge.
mechanism.reason: Defines edge-side composition of several owner responses.

invariant.owner_quote: Each downstream call carries its own deadline and authorization.
invariant.reason: Requires every downstream call to carry its own deadline and authorization.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: a gateway retry must not multiply load across every participant
failure_recovery.reason: Limits gateway retries so one failure does not multiply load across participants.

alternative.owner_quote: Client-side composition, a backend for frontend or an API Composition layer with a narrow contract may be preferable
alternative.reason: Names client composition, a backend for frontend or a narrow API composition layer.

mechanism.owner_quote: An edge can terminate TLS, validate tokens, compress, cache or enforce quotas before forwarding.

invariant.owner_quote: Offloading changes the trust boundary: downstream must receive an authenticated identity from a trusted intermediary and still enforce resource authorization.
invariant.reason: Bounds what the offloaded TLS endpoint identity proves.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: Header spoofing, confused-deputy paths and a proxy that becomes the only authorization point are common failures.

alternative.owner_quote: A service-mesh sidecar, application-level authorization or direct pass-through may be preferable when the edge cannot attest identity.

mechanism.owner_quote: A backend for frontend composes the API surface for one client experience. It needs a client owner, a composition contract, a policy for duplicated domain logic and a boundary that prevents the BFF from becoming a second domain authority.
mechanism.reason: Explains per-client composition and the ownership/contract boundary.

invariant.owner_quote: Do not use it when one API contract serves all clients or when the BFF would own core business rules.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: The failure path is drift between the BFF and the domain API; version the composition and test the client contract.
failure_recovery.reason: Names drift and prescribes versioning and client-contract testing.

alternative.owner_quote: A shared API with client-side selection is the alternative when the differences are small and can be expressed without a new authority.
alternative.reason: Names shared API plus client-side selection and the condition reversing the choice.

mechanism.owner_quote: An API composition layer calls several owner APIs for one request and assembles their responses into a single caller-visible result.
mechanism.reason: Defines query-time calls to several owner APIs and assembly of one caller-visible result.

invariant.owner_quote: The composed response must declare per-source freshness and what partial failure means, rather than presenting one aggregate result as uniformly current.
invariant.reason: Requires per-source freshness and an explicit partial-failure meaning.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: One slow or failed participant must not silently disappear from the result; apply per-call deadlines, mark missing parts or fail the composition explicitly.
failure_recovery.reason: Requires per-call deadlines, missing-part marking or explicit failure.

alternative.owner_quote: Build a maintained read model or a client-specific backend for frontend; prefer composition when the sources are authoritative and the caller needs a live view.
alternative.reason: Names a maintained read model or client-specific backend for frontend.

mechanism.owner_quote: A reverse proxy accepts client connections and forwards them to a selected backend, hiding topology and optionally terminating TLS.

invariant.owner_quote: It must define route identity, peer authentication, forwarded-header policy and backend failure behavior.
invariant.reason: Bounds what the proxy-terminated client identity establishes.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: Proxy bypass, stale routes and trusting a client-supplied identity header are common.

alternative.owner_quote: Direct service discovery, a gateway/BFF or a mesh sidecar may be preferable when the proxy adds a shared bottleneck without a required policy function.

mechanism.owner_quote: Service discovery may publish addresses plus eligibility metadata to a proxy or client.
mechanism.reason: Explains discovery as publishing addresses and eligibility metadata to a consumer.

invariant.owner_quote: If membership is stale, continued reachability still cannot establish write authority.
invariant.reason: Bounds what stale membership may authorize.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: Document who observes updates and how stale membership is detected. Distinguish the discovery control path from data-plane requests that can continue against a last-known usable set.
failure_recovery.reason: Requires stale-membership detection and separates the control path from last-known data-plane continuity.

alternative.owner_quote: Static DNS, a service mesh or direct endpoint configuration may be simpler when membership changes are rare.

mechanism.owner_quote: The caller obtains the membership view from a registry/control plane, caches it and selects a backend.

invariant.owner_quote: Stale membership can send traffic to a removed instance even when the address remains reachable.
invariant.reason: Applies the stale-membership safety rule to a client-held view as well.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: Bound the cache age, refresh budget and stale-cache alarm, and use a last-known set only for reads with an explicit freshness bound.
failure_recovery.reason: Requires the client-side observer to detect stale membership and bound continued data-plane use.

alternative.owner_quote: Static DNS, a service mesh or direct endpoint configuration may be simpler when membership changes are rare.

mechanism.owner_quote: A proxy, gateway or platform keeps the membership view and selects a backend for a stable virtual name.

invariant.owner_quote: Stale membership can keep a removed backend in the selection set even when the proxy is healthy.
invariant.reason: Applies the stale-membership safety rule to a proxy-held membership view.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: Proxy outage, retry amplification and a shared-proxy bottleneck are common; bound retries, expose a degraded path and plan the proxy's own failover.
failure_recovery.reason: Requires the proxy to detect stale membership and bound last-known data-plane use.

alternative.owner_quote: Static DNS, a service mesh or direct endpoint configuration may be simpler when membership changes are rare.
